title: Magnesium Ribbon Burning Lab with Temperature Curve & Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates an advanced chemistry lab experiment: burning a magnesium ribbon. The scene must expose all state through window.__3D_STATE__ for automated verification.

## Scene Setup
- Dark chemistry lab environment with a lab bench (a flat box geometry, dark grey).
- A clamp stand (thin cylinder + base) holding a magnesium ribbon (a narrow, shiny silver rectangular strip, ~0.3 units wide, ~3.0 units long, metallic material with roughness 0.3).
- A Bunsen burner mesh below the ribbon tip (cone + cylinder, blue-ish flame glow using a PointLight with color 0x3366ff, intensity 2).
- Camera at position (0, 4, 8) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light intensity 0.15 (dim lab). One directional light at (5,10,5) intensity 0.3.

## Chemistry / Physics Simulation
- The reaction is: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO.
- The magnesium ribbon has a mass of 2.4g (0.1 mol Mg). After complete combustion, MgO produced = 4.0g (0.1 mol MgO). Track these in state.
- Temperature model: ambient starts at 25°C. When ignited, the burn zone reaches up to 2500°C over ~4 seconds following a sigmoid curve, then cools back toward 200°C over ~10 seconds after burn completes.
- The ribbon burns from the bottom tip upward. Track burnProgress from 0.0 to 1.0. Burn duration = 6 seconds total once ignited.
- As the ribbon burns, produce bright white light: add a PointLight (color 0xffffff, intensity starting at 0 and ramping to 8 at peak, then fading). The light position follows the burn front.
- Produce MgO smoke: a simple particle system (50-100 small white spheres emitted upward from the burn front with slight random drift, fading opacity, removed after 3 seconds). Track activeParticleCount.
- The burned portion of the ribbon turns from silver to white MgO ash (change material color to 0xeeeeee, increase roughness to 0.9).
- Energy released: 1204 kJ/mol for 0.1 mol = 120.4 kJ total. Track energyReleased accumulating proportionally with burnProgress.

## Scoring System
- The user earns points for performing the experiment correctly in sequence:
  - +10 points: Wearing safety goggles (click goggles button before igniting)
  - +10 points: Recording initial mass (click 'Record Mass' button before igniting)
  - +20 points: Successfully igniting the ribbon
  - +30 points: Letting the burn complete fully (burnProgress reaches 1.0)
  - +15 points: Recording final mass after burn completes
  - +15 points: Calculating yield (click 'Calculate Yield' button after recording final mass)
- Maximum score = 100. Track score, and an array completedSteps[] of step names.
- Display score in a HUD panel top-right corner.

## User Interactions
- DOM button 'Toggle Goggles' (id='btn-goggles'): toggles safety goggles on/off. State: gogglesOn (boolean).
- DOM button 'Record Mass' (id='btn-record-mass'): records mass at current stage. Before burn: records initialMassRecorded=true. After burn complete: records finalMassRecorded=true.
- DOM button 'Ignite' (id='btn-ignite'): starts the burn IF goggles are on. If goggles off, set warningMessage='Put on safety goggles first!'. Sets ignited=true, reactionStartTime.
- DOM button 'Calculate Yield' (id='btn-calc-yield'): only works after finalMassRecorded. Computes theoreticalYield=4.0, actualYield=4.0*burnProgress, percentYield=(actualYield/theoreticalYield)*100. Sets yieldCalculated=true.
- DOM button 'Reset Experiment' (id='btn-reset'): resets all state to initial values, score=0, removes particles, resets ribbon.
- Keyboard 'T' toggles the temperature chart overlay visibility (a 2D canvas overlay or HTML div showing temperature vs time curve, id='temp-chart'). State: tempChartVisible (boolean).
- Keyboard 'P' pauses/resumes the simulation. State: paused (boolean).

## Temperature Chart
- A 2D overlay (HTML5 Canvas or styled div, id='temp-chart') positioned bottom-left, 300x200px.
- Plots temperature (Y-axis, 0-3000°C) vs time (X-axis, 0-20s).
- Draws data points in real-time as the experiment progresses. Red line for temperature curve.
- Show axis labels.

## HUD Elements
- Top-left: current temperature (id='hud-temp'), burn progress % (id='hud-progress'), reaction phase (id='hud-phase': 'idle'|'burning'|'cooling'|'complete').
- Top-right: score display (id='hud-score').
- Warning messages (id='hud-warning') shown for 3 seconds when triggered.
- All buttons in a panel (id='control-panel') on the right side.

## window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
{
  sceneReady: boolean,
  gogglesOn: boolean,
  ignited: boolean,
  paused: boolean,
  burnProgress: number (0.0-1.0),
  reactionPhase: string ('idle'|'burning'|'cooling'|'complete'),
  currentTemperature: number (°C),
  peakTemperature: number (max recorded °C),
  energyReleased: number (kJ, 0 to 120.4),
  mgMassRemaining: number (grams, starts 2.4, decreases),
  mgoMassProduced: number (grams, starts 0, increases to 4.0),
  activeParticleCount: number,
  burnLightIntensity: number,
  initialMassRecorded: boolean,
  finalMassRecorded: boolean,
  yieldCalculated: boolean,
  percentYield: number,
  score: number (0-100),
  completedSteps: string[],
  tempChartVisible: boolean,
  warningMessage: string,
  tempDataPoints: number (count of recorded data points),
  elapsedTime: number (seconds since ignition)
}
physics_constraints: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO stoichiometry: 2.4g Mg produces 4.0g MgO. Energy = 120.4 kJ total (1204 kJ/mol × 0.1 mol). Temperature follows sigmoid rise to ~2500°C over 4s then exponential decay toward 200°C. Mass conservation: mgMassRemaining + mgoMassProduced converted back should be consistent (total Mg atoms conserved). burnProgress monotonically increases from 0 to 1. Particle count >= 0 always. Temperature never negative or NaN. Energy monotonically increases during burn.
